response.overview: In folktales, babaylan are remembered as healers and spiritual mediums who belonged to the distant past. Babaylan sa Kanto begins with this belief, using images and sounds that evoke myth and memory before gradually revealing an asug living in the present. What first appears as legend is shown to exist within everyday life. The documentary offers an intimate look into the world of the asug, observing their routines, relationships, and spiritual practice, revealing how these traditions continue to shape everyday life.  At the heart of the film is the sisterhood they have built through shared purpose, care, and belonging. Their rituals and relationships transform an ordinary street into a sacred space where spirituality and community coexist. Through these lived experiences, Babaylan sa Kanto challenges the belief that babaylan exist only in folklore, revealing instead that they continue to live, adapt, and endure in the present.
response.title: Babaylan sa Kanto
